Then there is a recognizable set $B$ of finite lists of pairs of natural numbers, each of which is a graph, such that a partial recursive function $f$ is in $C$ if and only if some $\theta \in B$…
nodes.title: Effective Rice–Shapiro, necessity

nodes.summary: For every partial function $g : \mathbb{N} \rightharpoonup \mathbb{N}$ with finite domain there is a finite list $\theta$ of pairs of natural numbers such that the finite function of $\theta$ is $g$ and, for every pair $(x, y)$ in $\theta$, $g(x)$ is defined and equals $y$.
nodes.title: Finite-domain partial functions are finite functions

nodes.summary: For a finite list $\theta$ of pairs of natural numbers, the finite function of $\theta$ is the partial function $\mathbb{N} \rightharpoonup \mathbb{N}$ whose value at $x$ is the second component of the first pair in $\theta$ with first component $x$, and which is undefined at $x$ when $\theta$ has no pair with first component $x$.
nodes.title: Finite function of a list of pairs

nodes.summary: A finite list $\theta$ of pairs of natural numbers is a graph when, for every pair $(x, y)$ in $\theta$, the finite function of $\theta$ takes the value $y$ at $x$; that is, the first pair in $\theta$ with first component $x$ is $(x, y)$.
nodes.title: Graphs of finite functions

nodes.summary: The set of finite lists of pairs of natural numbers that are graphs is recursively enumerable.
nodes.title: Being a graph is recursively enumerable

nodes.summary: The set of pairs $(c, \theta)$, where $c$ is a code of a partial recursive function and $\theta$ is a finite list of pairs of natural numbers, such that for every pair $(x, y)$ in $\theta$ the function computed by $c$ is defined at $x$ with value $y$, is recursively enumerable.
nodes.title: Extending a finite list of pairs is recursively enumerable

nodes.summary: Every partial recursive member of a class with a recognizable index set has a partial recursive finite subfunction in the class.
nodes.title: Rice–Shapiro, finite approximation

nodes.summary: In a class with a recognizable index set, every partial recursive extension of a partial recursive member is a member.
nodes.title: Rice–Shapiro, upward closure

nodes.summary: A class of partial functions has a recognizable index set iff, among partial recursive functions, its members are exactly the extensions of the finite functions in some recognizable set of graphs.
nodes.title: The effective Rice–Shapiro theorem

Suppose that a partial recursive function $f$ is in $C$ if and only if some $\theta \in B$ satisfies: for every pair $(x, y)$ in $\theta$, $f(x)$ is defined and equals $y$. can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
